english: Let $N=\begin{pmatrix}4&6&1\\0&1&12\\0&0&9\end{pmatrix}$, and let $S$ denote the set of all $3\times3$ upper triangular matrices $X$ with real entries such that $X^{2}=N$. Then the least value of the sum of all the entries of $X$, as $X$ varies over $S$, is ______.
hindi: माना कि $N=\begin{pmatrix}4&6&1\\0&1&12\\0&0&9\end{pmatrix}$ है, तथा $S$ वास्तविक प्रविष्टियों वाले उन सभी $3\times3$ उपरि त्रिभुजीय आव्यूहों $X$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $X^{2}=N$ है। तब $X$ के $S$ में परिवर्तित होने पर $X$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों के योग का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: $a=\pm2,\ b=\pm1,\ c=\pm3$; then $a+b,\ b+c,\ a+c$ are never $0$, so $p=\dfrac{6}{a+b}$, $r=\dfrac{12}{b+c}$, $q=\dfrac{1-pr}{a+c}$: exactly $8$ matrices
solution_full: Let $X=\begin{pmatrix}a&p&q\\0&b&r\\0&0&c\end{pmatrix}$. The product of two upper triangular matrices is upper triangular, and row-by-column multiplication gives

Since $|a|,|b|,|c|$ are distinct, $a+b$, $b+c$, $a+c$ are never $0$. Hence $p(a+b)=6$, $r(b+c)=12$ and $q(a+c)+pr=1$ give unique $p=\dfrac{6}{a+b}$, $r=\dfrac{12}{b+c}$, $q=\dfrac{1-pr}{a+c}$ for each sign choice. So $S$ has exactly $8$ elements.
The least sum is $-18$, attained at $X=\begin{pmatrix}2&6&-19\\0&-1&-3\\0&0&-3\end{pmatrix}$; note that the choice with all diagonal entries negative gives only $-10$.
originality_note: New: all eight upper triangular square roots of a fixed triangular matrix are found and an extremal entry sum is asked; the minimum is not at the all-negative diagonal (way 3, a family fixed by two conditions). Closest known: a qualifying-exam exercise asking for one square root of an upper triangular matrix with diagonal 1, 4, 9. Different because: the diagonal and off-diagonal data were changed after the search, and the question needs every root and a comparison across the eight sign cases.

concept_use.Special types of square matrices: X is upper triangular, so X^2 is upper triangular with diagonal a^2, b^2, c^2; this reduces X^2 = N to the sign choices a = +-2, b = +-1, c = +-3.
concept_use.Matrix Multiplication & Algebraic Proper: Row-by-column multiplication gives the off-diagonal equations p(a+b) = 6, r(b+c) = 12, q(a+c) + pr = 1 that fix p, r, q.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy solves X^2 = N for upper triangular X and returns exactly 8 solutions, with sums 10, -17, 9, -18, 18, -9, 17, -10; the least is -18 (a negative integer, as planned). Changed: the first design used diagonal 1, 4, 9, which resembled a published exercise, so N was redesigned.
key_step: Expressing the off-diagonal entries in terms of the diagonal signs and comparing all eight cases.
justification: Two ideas (triangular structure of X^2 and solving the coupled off-diagonal equations) with eight-case exact casework and no options; the trap that the all-negative choice is not least keeps it at 3. Comparable to the matrix identity work of 2021-P1-Q14 (L3); lighter than the counting of 2024-P1-Q10 (L4).
